content.content:
1	# Agent harness and tool calling
2	
3	How the one agent loop runs, how each tool call is checked, and what happens when something goes wrong. The product
4	rules (one loop, no limits, plain-text answers, approvals) are in [the agent](agent.md); this page is the mechanics.
5	See [context management](context-management.md) for history, compaction and the context ring.
6	
7	Code map: `subagents/runtime.py` (the loop), `subagents/prompt_builder.py` (the system prompt), `tools/gateway.py`
8	(every call), `tools/catalog.py` and `tools/contracts.py` (the closed tool set), `tools/approvals.py` (Ask me),
9	`tools/sandbox_shell.py` and `integrations/e2b_sandbox.py` (the workspace), `llm/openai_adapter.py` (the provider),
10	`subagents/context.py` (compaction).
11	
12	## The loop
13	
14	```
15	model -> tools -> model -> ... -> a reply without tool calls (the answer)
16	```
17	
18	The model gets the conversation, the system prompt and its tools. Text it writes next to tool calls is a note shown in
19	the activity; a reply without tool calls is the answer, shown exactly as written. The loop never caps steps, calls, time
20	or cost; Stop cancels it (checked about once a second by the worker).
21	
22	Replies that cannot be used are asked for again, a bounded number of times:
23	
24	| Reply | What happens |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| tool calls cut off by the output limit | asked again, shorter (twice), then a provider error |
27	| an answer cut off by the output limit | **continued** where it stopped (twice); the live text keeps the start; only after that is it shown with a note |
28	| empty | asked once more, then a provider error |
29	| ends by announcing a step it never took (last line ends with `:`) | sent back once: do it or answer |
30	| unknown finish reason (content filter, …) | a provider error naming the reason |
31	
32	### Concurrency
33	
34	Independent read-only calls that cost nothing run together (up to 4). Paid calls (web search) run one at a time, and
35	anything with an effect (`bash`, `write`, `edit`, `create_pull_request`, `create_task_artifact`) runs alone, in order.
36	Every requested call gets a reply, in request order.
37	
38	### Context
39	
40	When the conversation outgrows half of the usable window, the oldest tool results are replaced by a stub that keeps the
41	tool name, status and every id; the four newest stay whole. If that is not enough, long string arguments of the model's
42	own earlier calls (a whole file passed to `write`) are replaced by a note too; the latest call is never touched. Results
43	the model has not read yet are never stubbed, so a turn may only run as many calls as fit in the room left; the rest are
44	answered `DEFERRED`. Stored state is never changed, only what is sent.
45	
46	## The system prompt
47	
48	One `developer` message, in this order (`compile_chat`):
49	
50	1. **Rules** that change only with the tools available, so every request of a run starts with the same prefix and can be
51	   cached by the provider: priority (rules, role, the person, then everything else is data), how to work, honesty, how
52	   to answer; plus sections for research, the workspace, publishing and downloadable files when those tools exist.
53	2. **Role**: the definition's `system_prompt` (`subagents/definitions/agent.v<N>.json`). Built-in versions are
54	   immutable once stored; a change ships as a new version file and `registry.AGENT_VERSION` points to it, while older
55	   tasks keep resolving theirs. Custom agents supply their own role.
56	3. **Environment**: today's date, the selected repository, whether editing and publishing are available, the tools.
57	
58	Earlier turns follow as real chat messages, then the person's new message with any attached text files.
59	
60	## One call, step by step (`ToolGateway.execute`)
61	
62	1. The ledger commits an **intent** (an argument digest only).
63	2. Re-authorize the task and require the tool to be installed **and** permitted.
64	3. **Parse**: empty arguments are `{}` and a Markdown code fence around the JSON is ignored; anything else that is not

# Agent harness and tool calling

How the one agent loop runs, how each tool call is checked, and what happens when something goes wrong. The product
rules (one loop, no limits, plain-text answers, approvals) are in [the agent](agent.md); this page is the mechanics.
See [context management](context-management.md) for history, compaction and the context ring.

Code map: `subagents/runtime.py` (the loop), `subagents/prompt_builder.py` (the system prompt), `tools/gateway.py`
(every call), `tools/catalog.py` and `tools/contracts.py` (the closed tool set), `tools/approvals.py` (Ask me),
`tools/sandbox_shell.py` and `integrations/e2b_sandbox.py` (the workspace), `llm/openai_adapter.py` (the provider),
`subagents/context.py` (compaction).

## The loop

```
model -> tools -> model -> ... -> a reply without tool calls (the answer)
```

The model gets the conversation, the system prompt and its tools. Text it writes next to tool calls is a note shown in
the activity; a reply without tool calls is the answer, shown exactly as written. The loop never caps steps, calls, time
or cost; Stop cancels it (checked about once a second by the worker).

Replies that cannot be used are asked for again, a bounded number of times:

| Reply | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| tool calls cut off by the output limit | asked again, shorter (twice), then a provider error |
| an answer cut off by the output limit | **continued** where it stopped (twice); the live text keeps the start; only after that is it shown with a note |
| empty | asked once more, then a provider error |
| ends by announcing a step it never took (last line ends with `:`) | sent back once: do it or answer |
| unknown finish reason (content filter, …) | a provider error naming the reason |

### Concurrency

Independent read-only calls that cost nothing run together (up to 4). Paid calls (web search) run one at a time, and
anything with an effect (`bash`, `write`, `edit`, `create_pull_request`, `create_task_artifact`) runs alone, in order.
Every requested call gets a reply, in request order.

### Context

When the conversation outgrows half of the usable window, the oldest tool results are replaced by a stub that keeps the
tool name, status and every id; the four newest stay whole. If that is not enough, long string arguments of the model's
own earlier calls (a whole file passed to `write`) are replaced by a note too; the latest call is never touched. Results
the model has not read yet are never stubbed, so a turn may only run as many calls as fit in the room left; the rest are
answered `DEFERRED`. Stored state is never changed, only what is sent.

   immutable once stored; a change ships as a new version file and `registry.AGENT_VERSION` points to it, while older
   tasks keep resolving theirs. Custom agents supply their own role.

1	# The agent
2	
3	One loop serves every message: the model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools; it calls tools until it
4	has what it needs, then answers in plain text. That text is the answer, exactly as written
5	(`apps/api/src/agentforge/subagents/runtime.py`).
6	
7	## What was removed, and why
8	
9	Earlier versions ran a router, a planner, stage agents and an independent verifier, and forced every run to end by
10	submitting a typed result with evidence. A reply that did not satisfy those rules was rewritten as `PARTIAL`, so a
11	plain "What would you like help with?" showed a "Partial result" banner. All of that is gone: no router, planner,
12	verifier, `submit_result`, `PARTIAL` status or run-details page. A run ends as:
13	
14	| Outcome | When | Shown |
15	| --- | --- | --- |
16	| `COMPLETED` | the model answered | its text, as written |
17	| `FAILED` | the provider or a tool broke | the reason: a provider's own message, credentials removed |
18	| `CANCELLED` | the person pressed Stop | "Stopped." |
19	
20	Older messages may still carry `PARTIAL`; they render as plain text.
21	
22	## Limits
23	
24	Nothing caps steps, tool calls, cost or time. Usage is still recorded for accounting, and Stop always works. The
25	numbers in the budget rows (`Budget`, `UNLIMITED_*`) exist because the ledger needs positive values; they are set
26	high enough never to refuse anything.
27	
28	## Tools
29	
30	| Group | Tools |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| Web | `web_search`, `fetch_webpage` |
33	| Repository (read only, pinned commit) | `list_repo_files`, `search_repo`, `read_repo_file`, `get_issue`, `get_pr_status` |
34	| Sandbox (needs `E2B_API_KEY`) | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, `ls` |
35	| Pull request (needs GitHub App + `ENABLE_GITHUB_WRITES`) | `create_pull_request` |
36	| Files and history | `create_task_artifact`, `read_task_artifact`, `search_conversation_history`, `read_context_resource` |
37	| Skills (when the person has any switched on) | `use_skill`: loads a playbook by name; see [skills](skills.md) |
38	| Plugins (per conversation) | `slug__tool`, from the MCP servers the person connected; see [plugins](plugins.md) |
39	
40	The sandbox (`integrations/e2b_sandbox.py`, `tools/sandbox_shell.py`) is created on first use and kept for the
41	conversation: files and installed packages stay between messages. It has internet access and holds no secrets. When a
42	repository is selected the backend uploads its pinned commit and commits it as `agentforge-base`; pull requests are opened
43	by the backend from `git diff agentforge-base`, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox.
44	
45	## Approvals
46	
47	A global setting (`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/approval-mode`, default `ask`) applies to every conversation.
48	
49	* **Ask me**: before `bash`, `write`, `edit` or `create_pull_request` the run stops and the chat shows an Approve /
50	  Decline card (`approval.required`) with exactly what will run: the whole command, the file content or the edit, or
51	  the pull request with every file it changes. It waits as long as it takes. Declining returns a normal tool result
52	  telling the agent the person said no. A command too long to show in full is refused before anyone is asked.

# The agent

One loop serves every message: the model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools; it calls tools until it
has what it needs, then answers in plain text. That text is the answer, exactly as written
(`apps/api/src/agentforge/subagents/runtime.py`).

## What was removed, and why

Earlier versions ran a router, a planner, stage agents and an independent verifier, and forced every run to end by
submitting a typed result with evidence. A reply that did not satisfy those rules was rewritten as `PARTIAL`, so a
plain "What would you like help with?" showed a "Partial result" banner. All of that is gone: no router, planner,
verifier, `submit_result`, `PARTIAL` status or run-details page. A run ends as:

| Outcome | When | Shown |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMPLETED` | the model answered | its text, as written |
| `FAILED` | the provider or a tool broke | the reason: a provider's own message, credentials removed |
| `CANCELLED` | the person pressed Stop | "Stopped." |

Older messages may still carry `PARTIAL`; they render as plain text.

## Limits

Nothing caps steps, tool calls, cost or time. Usage is still recorded for accounting, and Stop always works. The
numbers in the budget rows (`Budget`, `UNLIMITED_*`) exist because the ledger needs positive values; they are set
high enough never to refuse anything.

## Tools

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Web | `web_search`, `fetch_webpage` |
| Repository (read only, pinned commit) | `list_repo_files`, `search_repo`, `read_repo_file`, `get_issue`, `get_pr_status` |
| Sandbox (needs `E2B_API_KEY`) | `bash`, `read`, `write`, `edit`, `grep`, `find`, `ls` |
| Pull request (needs GitHub App + `ENABLE_GITHUB_WRITES`) | `create_pull_request` |
| Files and history | `create_task_artifact`, `read_task_artifact`, `search_conversation_history`, `read_context_resource` |
| Skills (when the person has any switched on) | `use_skill`: loads a playbook by name; see [skills](skills.md) |
| Plugins (per conversation) | `slug__tool`, from the MCP servers the person connected; see [plugins](plugins.md) |

The sandbox (`integrations/e2b_sandbox.py`, `tools/sandbox_shell.py`) is created on first use and kept for the
conversation: files and installed packages stay between messages. It has internet access and holds no secrets. When a
repository is selected the backend uploads its pinned commit and commits it as `agentforge-base`; pull requests are opened
by the backend from `git diff agentforge-base`, so GitHub credentials never enter the sandbox.

## Approvals

A global setting (`GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/approval-mode`, default `ask`) applies to every conversation.

* **Ask me**: before `bash`, `write`, `edit` or `create_pull_request` the run stops and the chat shows an Approve /
  Decline card (`approval.required`) with exactly what will run: the whole command, the file content or the edit, or
  the pull request with every file it changes. It waits as long as it takes. Declining returns a normal tool result
  telling the agent the person said no. A command too long to show in full is refused before anyone is asked.
* **Approve for me**: nothing asks.

A plugin tool also asks in **Ask me** mode unless its server declares it read-only.

The mode is read before each call, so switching it releases a waiting card. Answers: `POST /api/v1/tool-approvals/{id}`.
Implementation: `tools/approvals.py`, hooked into `tools/gateway.py`.

`next_line`), and its limits. Every argument in `tools/contracts.py` has a `description`. Provider schemas drop

returns an error code, a short detail written by our own code and static guidance from `error_guidance`. Adding a tool
means adding its argument model, a description, its capability in `contracts/agent_definition.py`, and a label in
`apps/web/lib/tool-steps.ts`. See [the harness](agent-harness.md) for the whole tool-calling contract.

Run events become one timeline shared by the live view and finished replies: each tool call with a short detail (the

or file content. While a run is active the thread shows the steps; once the answer arrives they fold into a

1	# Conversation context and composer status
2	
3	The current automatic-conversation path adds source-linked incremental summaries,
4	retrieval of originals, and execution-time snapshots. See
5	[conversation reliability](conversation-reliability.md) for the current delivery,
6	history and deployment contracts. The extractive policy below remains the legacy
7	standalone compatibility path.
8	
9	Reviewed 2026-10-11. This covers the request path from conversation admission to
10	provider accounting and the composer. It does not qualify a hosted deployment
11	or million-token live workload.
12	
13	## Model capacity and cost
14	
15	OpenAI's [Luna model documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-luna)
16	specifies a 1,050,000-token total window, a 922,000-token input limit and a
17	128,000-token maximum output. AgentForge reserves its configured output allowance
18	and uses the smaller of the remaining window and the provider input limit. Smaller
19	operator windows continue to work. Luna's Chat Completions endpoint takes function
20	calls only without reasoning, so requests at effort `none` use it, as before, and every
21	other effort (the person's choice in the composer, High by default) is sent through the
22	Responses endpoint, which keeps tools with reasoning. The runtime still speaks the chat
23	message format: the adapter translates the history and the reply (`llm/openai_adapter.py`).
24	
25	Luna installations with an input allowance above 272,000 require these explicit
26	settings in addition to the standard input/output rates:
27	
28	```dotenv
29	LLM_CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS=1050000
30	LLM_LONG_CONTEXT_INPUT_USD_PER_MILLION=0.20
31	LLM_LONG_CONTEXT_OUTPUT_USD_PER_MILLION=0.75
32	```
33	
34	These are the Standard rates reviewed on the date above; verify them against the
35	[official pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing) before
36	deployment. Long-context pricing applies to the entire request when measured
37	input exceeds 272,000. Cache discounts are conservatively ignored. Missing long
38	rates fail closed. Increasing capacity never increases the task's spending,
39	time, permission, or tool-call grants.
40	
41	Request fitting uses an upper-biased local text estimate, not an exact tokenizer:
42	three ASCII characters per token, two tokens per Unicode code point, plus protocol
43	and message overhead. Authorization uses a separate UTF-8 byte bound, capped by
44	the effective provider input limit, and the appropriate price tier. This avoids
45	treating a prose heuristic as a monetary upper bound for dense code. Final charges
46	use provider-reported input/output tokens. Unknown usage retains its reservation.
47	Exact model-side input counting and opaque provider compaction would require a
48	Responses adapter and a separate protocol/accounting qualification; they are not
49	represented as already implemented here.
50	
51	## What carries into the next message
52	
53	Each turn starts new specialist working contexts. It receives the current goal,
54	attachments, and an immutable, task-owned history extract through paged tools.
55	The next turn does not append the previous run's tool transcript.
56	
57	The HTTP conversation path shares the same history policy with the status API:
58	approximately a tenth of usable input, capped at 48,000 serialized UTF-8 bytes.
59	The cap bounds read pages, storage, latency, and cost even for a million-token
60	model. Standalone repository callers retain the 7,500-byte compatibility default.
61	
62	The extract considers the latest 40 stored messages. Up to 12 recent messages are
63	included in full when they fit, and up to 12 earlier messages have short attributed
64	excerpts. Space is reserved for those earlier excerpts. A shortened message keeps
65	both its opening and ending and is explicitly marked `truncated`; whitespace in
66	complete originals is preserved. Message IDs, sequence, and role retain provenance.
67	Full originals stay stored and available through owner-scoped message pagination.
68	This is deterministic excerpting, not a model-generated semantic memory. Details
69	outside the extract are not implicitly recalled by the harness.
70	
71	Coding executors and both independent reviewers also receive the complete owned
72	goal, attachments and saved history extract in a separate bounded user-role data
73	message. Short planning previews cannot silently remove the end of a long goal or
74	the supplied attachments. This data is never a developer instruction and grants
75	no additional tools or repository access. The provider fitting and cost checks
76	include it, and its contents are included in the recorded brief fingerprint.
77	
78	The v4 router has enough bounded steps/tool calls for paged history plus all
79	attachment inputs. Released v3 definitions remain intact. Its logical routing
80	operation ID stays stable so recovery reuses a completed earlier result rather
81	than repeating paid work. History, attachments, excerpts and tool results remain
82	lower-trust data; they cannot grant repository access or override platform rules.
83	
84	## Within a run
85	
86	At half of usable input the runtime shortens already-read old tool results. A
87	hard fitting pass can shorten more when needed. The platform prompt, assignment,
88	goal/attachment/history reads, and the latest unread tool batch remain intact.
89	Tool-call/result pairing is preserved. Compacted results retain tool/status,
90	evidence/artifact IDs, and bounded file identity and paging metadata. Their original
91	content remains persisted; rereads still pass the same ownership/permission checks.
92	
93	The full serialized conversation is recounted after shortening, including JSON
94	escaping. Space for a tool batch includes worst-case dense Unicode and deferred
95	reply overhead. Unaffordable-to-fit calls are deferred before execution. A forced
96	typed partial result remains the fallback when context, budget, time or step limits
97	prevent further work. Large previews are bounded by their final encoded envelope.
98	
99	## What the composer reports
100	
101	The small indicator opens on hover, click, or keyboard activation. It does not
102	disable sending or interfere with repository selection, model selection,
103	attachments, or stop controls. Touch retains an enlarged target.
104	
105	The headline is an **estimated next-message input**: instruction/tool overhead,
106	the actual next history extract, and the unsent draft/attachments. The denominator
107	is the effective input allowance. The compact card shows only the percentage,
108	meter and token estimate; it has no expandable diagnostics or model/settings
109	breakdown. Empty, unknown, loading, stale, error, and near-limit states remain
110	distinct. Detailed usage and history coverage remain in the API response.
111	
112	The popup is centered directly above the context indicator with a fixed 6px gap
113	from its button. Its distance does not grow with the text area's height. It flips
114	vertically when needed and shifts away from screen edges without falling back to
115	a distant side of the composer. Pointer opening does not move focus into the
116	popup; keyboard opening supports focus and Escape dismissal.
117	
118	The latest run's provider-measured peak remains separate. It can include several
119	independent agents and is never added to the next draft or used to recommend a new
120	conversation. API coverage describes included text, not proof of model consumption.
121	Actual input read receipts remain independently verified by the harness.
122	
123	Polling is sequential, times out, pauses when hidden, resumes on visibility, aborts
124	on conversation changes, and preserves only the last successful value for the
125	same conversation. A failed refresh is explicitly shown as stale. No provider
126	requests occur when viewing context status or typing a draft.
127	
128	## Validation
129	
130	`scripts/release_checks.py` includes backend unit checks, disposable PostgreSQL
131	fixtures, frontend context projection regressions, lint, types and build. Focused
132	regressions cover Luna limits and price thresholds, serialized multilingual
133	history bounds, truncation provenance, pinned/unread results, draft projections,
134	reply reservations, and preserving the 1.05M capacity in number formatting.
135

5	replaced by a stub that keeps the tool name, status and every evidence/artifact id, so citations stay
6	valid, while the results the model is still working from stay in full. The stored conversation is
7	never altered; only what is sent to the model is compacted.
8	
9	Results the model has not read yet (the latest tool turn) are never stubbed: stubbing them would hide
10	data the run just paid for while its consumption receipts say it was read. The runtime instead limits
11	how many results a turn may request, so the latest batch always fits.
12	"""

23	# these makes the model forget what it was asked, so they are never stubbed however full the window is.
24	PINNED_TOOLS = frozenset({"read_task_input"})
25	STUB_NOTE = ("Full result removed to save space; the ids below remain valid. "

27	             "repeating the original paid or effectful operation. Otherwise use an authorized source read.")

31	    return message_input_tokens(messages)
32

34	def _stub(message: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
35	    content = message.get("content")
36	    if not isinstance(content, str) or not content.startswith(RESULT_PREFIX):
37	        return None
38	    try:
39	        original = json.loads(content[len(RESULT_PREFIX):])
40	    except ValueError:
41	        original = {}
42	    kept = {key: original[key] for key in ("tool", "status", "error_code", "evidence_ids", "artifact_ids") if key in original}
43	    data = original.get("data")
44	    if isinstance(data, dict):
45	        # Keep navigation and identity, so a compacted read can be resumed or fetched again.
46	        # Content is deliberately not promoted to a generated summary or trusted instruction.
47	        anchors = {key: data[key] for key in ("id", "resource_id", "path", "sha256", "content_sha256", "offset",

83	        return messages
84	    tool_positions = [index for index, message in enumerate(messages) if message.get("role") == "tool"]
85	    protected = latest_batch(messages) | pinned_results(messages) | (set(tool_positions[-keep_recent:]) if keep_recent else set())
86	    compacted = list(messages)
87	    for index in tool_positions:
88	        if index in protected:
89	            continue
90	        stub = _stub(compacted[index])
91	        if stub is None:
92	            continue
93	        compacted[index] = stub
94	        # Recount the serialized envelope, including escaping. Subtracting raw content estimates
95	        # can claim a request fits when JSON backslashes and role boundaries say otherwise.
96	        total = conversation_tokens(compacted)
97	        if total <= limit_tokens:
98	            return compacted
99	    # Still too big: the model's own earlier calls can carry whole files (write) or long scripts. Once acted on, their
100	    # long text values are only a record; the file itself is the current truth. The latest call is never touched.
101	    assistants = [index for index, message in enumerate(compacted) if message.get("role") == "assistant"]
102	    for index in assistants[:-1]:
103	        slim = _slim_calls(compacted[index])
104	        if slim is None:
105	            continue
106	        compacted[index] = slim
107	        if conversation_tokens(compacted) <= limit_tokens:
108	            break
109	    return compacted
110	
111	
112	def _slim_calls(message: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
113	    """The message with long string arguments of its tool calls replaced by a note, or None when nothing is long."""
114	    calls, changed = [], False
115	    for call in message.get("tool_calls") or []:
116	        function = call.get("function") if isinstance(call, dict) else None
117	        raw = function.get("arguments") if isinstance(function, dict) else None
118	        if isinstance(raw, str) and len(raw) > LONG_ARGUMENTS_CHARS:
119	            try:
120	                data = json.loads(raw)
121	            except ValueError:
122	                data = None
123	            if isinstance(data, dict):
124	                data = {key: (f"[{len(value)} characters omitted to save space; read the file for its current content]"
125	                              if isinstance(value, str) and len(value) > 200 else value) for key, value in data.items()}
126	                call = {**call, "function": {**function, "arguments": json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)}}
127	                changed = True
128	        calls.append(call)
129	    return {**message, "tool_calls": calls} if changed else None

1	"""One reusable LangGraph agent loop for built-in and custom definitions.
2	
3	How an agent works:
4	- The model gets the conversation, a system prompt and its tools. It calls tools until it has what it needs and then
5	  answers in plain text. That text, exactly as written, is the answer: nothing wraps it, grades it or turns it into a
6	  status.
7	- A tool error is returned to the model as a normal tool result naming what was wrong, so it can correct itself.
8	- Independent read-only calls in one turn run side by side, and so do delegations (each subagent has its own run and ledger);
9	  any other call with an effect runs alone.
10	- Old tool results are compacted when the conversation outgrows the model's window. If it still cannot fit, the
11	  provider's own limit is what the person is told.
12	- Main conversations keep their existing Stop behavior. Delegated children have a wall-time bound and ledger-enforced operation/cost bounds.
13	"""
14	
15	import asyncio
16	import inspect
17	import json
18	from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
19	from typing import Any, TypedDict
20

25	from agentforge.contracts.subagent import SubagentResult
26	from agentforge.contracts.tasks import MAX_ANSWER_CHARS
27	from agentforge.llm.models import ModelContextLimit, ModelProviderError, ToolCallingModel, conservative_input_tokens
28	from agentforge.tools.catalog import error_guidance
29	from agentforge.tools.gateway import ToolGateway
30	from agentforge.tools.lifecycle import legacy_call_id

35	from .scope import EffectiveScope, TaskContext

37	# A reply cut off by the output limit while it was calling tools is asked for again, shorter, this many times.
38	MAX_CUTOFF_RETRIES = 2
39	CUTOFF_NOTICE = ("Your last reply was cut off by the output length limit, so none of it was used. Write it again, shorter: "
40	                 "summarise instead of listing everything, and keep any file content within about 3000 words.")
41	EMPTY_NOTICE = "Your last reply was empty. Reply to the user now."
42	CUT_OFF_NOTE = "\n\n[The model's reply was cut off by its output length limit.]"
43	# A final answer that reached the output limit is continued this many times before it is shown with CUT_OFF_NOTE.
44	MAX_CONTINUATIONS = 2
45	CONTINUE_NOTICE = "Your reply reached the output length limit. Continue it exactly where it stopped, without repeating anything."
46	# A reply that ends by announcing a next step ("Let me check the tests:") but makes no tool call has stopped too early.
47	STALLED_NOTICE = ("Your last message announced a next step but made no tool call, so nothing happened. Do it now, or give your "
48	                  "final answer if you are done.")
49	RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES = 16000
50	# A rendered tool result is capped near 16 KB, which is about this many tokens. A turn may only request as
51	# many results as fit in the room left in the window.
52	RESULT_TOKENS = RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES + 1000  # includes dense Unicode, JSON escaping and tool-message overhead
53	# LangGraph needs a finite recursion limit; this is far beyond any real run.
54	RECURSION_LIMIT = 1_000_000
55	# A text value cut to make a result fit keeps at least this much: below it, cutting loses more than it saves.
56	MIN_KEPT_CHARS = 200
57	OMITTED_MARK = "…[{} characters omitted]"
58	
59	
60	class ChildState(TypedDict):
61	    messages: list[dict[str, Any]]
62	    pending: list[dict[str, Any]]
63	    steps: int
64	    cuts: int      # replies cut off by the output limit so far
65	    empties: int   # empty replies so far
66	    answer: str | None
67	    partial: str   # the start of an answer that reached the output limit and is being continued
68	    conts: int     # continuations asked for so far
69	    nudged: bool   # a stalled reply was already sent back once
70	
71	
72	def stalled(text: str) -> bool:
73	    """The reply ends by introducing something that never came: its last line ends with a colon."""
74	    last = text.rstrip().rsplit("\n", 1)[-1].strip()
75	    return last.endswith(":") and not last.startswith(("|", "#", "-", "*", ">")) and len(last) < 300
76	
77	
78	def fit_result(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
79	    """`payload` rendered within RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES by cutting its data's longest text values first, or None when that
80	    cannot make it fit (many short values), for the caller's cruder preview.
81	
82	    Every key stays, so cursors (next_offset, next_line) and ids still work, and a note says where the full result is.
83	    The outcome itself is not changed.
84	    """
85	    data = json.loads(json.dumps(payload["data"], ensure_ascii=False))
86	    leaves: list[list[Any]] = []  # [container, key, original text, characters kept]
87	
88	    def collect(node: Any) -> None:
89	        items = node.items() if isinstance(node, dict) else enumerate(node) if isinstance(node, list) else ()
90	        for key, value in items:
91	            if isinstance(value, str):
92	                leaves.append([node, key, value, len(value)])
93	            else:
94	                collect(value)
95	    collect(data)
96	    reference = data.get("resource_id")
97	    note = "This result was too long to show whole, so its longest text values were cut where marked."
98	    if isinstance(reference, str):
99	        note += (f' Read the full result with read_context_resource(resource_id="{reference}", offset=0) when that tool is '
100	                 "available, continuing from its next_offset; this does not repeat the original call.")
101	    for _ in range(200):
102	        rendered = json.dumps({**payload, "data": {**data, "preview_truncated": True, "preview_note": note}},
103	                              ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
104	        excess = len(rendered.encode()) - RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES
105	        if excess <= 0:
106	            return rendered
107	        leaf = max(leaves, key=lambda item: item[3], default=None)
108	        if leaf is None or leaf[3] <= MIN_KEPT_CHARS:
109	            return None
110	        container, key, original, kept = leaf
111	        # Characters to drop for `excess` bytes at this value's own bytes per character (escaping, Unicode), plus the mark.
112	        size = len(json.dumps(original[:kept], ensure_ascii=False).encode())
113	        leaf[3] = kept = max(MIN_KEPT_CHARS, kept - int(excess * kept / max(1, size)) - 40)
114	        container[key] = original[:kept] + OMITTED_MARK.format(len(original) - kept)
115	    return None
116	
117	
118	class ChildRuntime:
119	    async def run(self, *, definition: AgentDefinition, ctx: TaskContext,
120	                  scope: EffectiveScope, model: ToolCallingModel, gateway: ToolGateway,
121	                  budgets: BudgetService, reservation: Reservation,
122	                  messages: list[dict[str, Any]], resources: ResourceResolver,
123	                  reauthorize: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
124	                  config: RunnableConfig | None = None, stream=None) -> SubagentResult:
125	        schemas = gateway.schemas()
126	
127	        def drop_live() -> None:
128	            """Whatever the sink shows is not going to be used (an attempt thrown away, a run that failed): clear it."""
129	            discard = getattr(stream, "discard", None)
130	            if discard is not None:
131	                discard()
132	
133	        # Models that retry a broken stream themselves say so by taking `on_retry`; others are simply not told.
134	        accepts_retry = "on_retry" in inspect.signature(model.complete).parameters
135	        accepts_tool = "on_tool" in inspect.signature(model.complete).parameters
136	        context_budget = getattr(model, "context_budget_tokens", None)
137	        max_input = getattr(model, "max_input_tokens", None)
138	
139	        def room_left(conversation: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int | None:
140	            """Input tokens still free once every result the model has already read is stubbed out."""
141	            if not max_input:
142	                return None
143	            return max_input - conservative_input_tokens(compact_messages(conversation, 1, 0), schemas)
144	
145	        def fit(conversation: list[dict[str, Any]]):
146	            """The messages to send and their cost bound: compact gently, then harder, until the request fits."""
147	            for keep in (KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS, 1, 0):
148	                sent = compact_messages(conversation, context_budget if keep == KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS else 1, keep)
149	                try:
150	                    return sent, model.maximum_request_cost(sent, schemas)
151	                except ModelContextLimit:
152	                    continue
153	            return None
154	
155	        async def call_model(state: ChildState) -> dict[str, Any]:
156	            await reauthorize()
157	            budgets.check_active(reservation.id)
158	            steps = state["steps"]
159	            conversation = state["messages"]
160	            fitted = fit(conversation)
161	            if fitted is None:
162	                raise ModelContextLimit("The conversation no longer fits in the model's context window, even with old tool results removed.")
163	            sent, bound = fitted
164	            stubbed = [kept.get("tool_call_id") for original, kept in zip(conversation, sent)
165	                       if original is not kept and kept.get("role") == "tool"]
166	            operation_key = f"{reservation.run_id}:model:{steps}"
167	            auditor = getattr(resources, "record_provider_input", None)
168	            if auditor is not None:
169	                await auditor(ctx, operation_key, sent, schemas)
170	            budgets.authorize_operation(reservation.id, operation_key, bound, kind="model")
171	            extra: dict[str, Any] = {}
172	            partial = state["partial"]
173	            broken = 0
174	
175	            def restart() -> None:
176	                # A new attempt (or a retried, broken one) starts from the part of the answer already written.
177	                stream.begin()
178	                if partial:
179	                    stream.feed(partial)
180	
181	            def retried() -> None:
182	                # A stream that broke midway was billed for what it produced, which the provider never reported, so the
183	                # ledger records that attempt as its own operation of unknown cost before the request is sent again.
184	                nonlocal broken
185	                broken += 1
186	                key = f"{operation_key}:broken:{broken}"
187	                budgets.authorize_operation(reservation.id, key, bound, kind="model")
188	                budgets.record_usage(reservation.id, key, None)
189	                if stream is not None:
190	                    restart()
191	            if accepts_retry:
192	                extra["on_retry"] = retried
193	            if stream is not None:
194	                extra["on_text"] = stream.feed
195	                extra["on_narration"] = stream.feed_narration
196	                if accepts_tool and getattr(stream, "feed_tool", None) is not None:
197	                    # A call is shown as the model writes it, under the id its tool.started event will carry.
198	                    extra["on_tool"] = lambda index, provider_id, name, piece: stream.feed_tool(
199	                        index, legacy_call_id(f"{reservation.run_id}:tool:{provider_id}"), name, piece)
200	                restart()
201	            try:
202	                response = await model.complete(sent, schemas, **extra)
203	            except BaseException:
204	                budgets.record_usage(reservation.id, operation_key, None)
205	                drop_live()
206	                raise
207	            # The call succeeded, so its real cost is recorded before anything else can fail: `end` may raise an event
208	            # error the sink deferred (a stopped run, a lost lease), which must not charge the call's upper bound.
209	            budgets.record_usage(reservation.id, operation_key, response.usage.cost_usd,
210	                usage={"input_tokens": response.usage.input_tokens,
211	                       "output_tokens": response.usage.output_tokens, "compacted_results": len(stubbed),
212	                       "configured_model": model.model_id, "reported_model": response.model_id})
213	            if stream is not None:
214	                try:
215	                    stream.end()
216	                except BaseException:
217	                    drop_live()
218	                    raise
219	            message = response.message
220	            if len(json.dumps(message, allow_nan=False).encode()) > 4 * MAX_ANSWER_CHARS or message.get("role") != "assistant":
221	                raise ModelProviderError("invalid model response envelope")
222	            pending = message.get("tool_calls") or []
223	            if not isinstance(pending, list):
224	                raise ModelProviderError("invalid model tool calls")
225	            if len({call.get("id") for call in pending if isinstance(call, dict)}) != len(pending):
226	                raise ModelProviderError("duplicate model tool call identifiers")
227	            reason = response.finish_reason
228	            if reason == "length" and pending:
229	                # Cut off while writing tool calls: their arguments are unusable. Ask again, shorter.
230	                drop_live()
231	                if state["cuts"] >= MAX_CUTOFF_RETRIES:
232	                    raise ModelProviderError("The model kept running out of output space while calling tools.", detail="finish_reason: length")
233	                return {"messages": [*conversation, {"role": "user", "content": CUTOFF_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
234	                        "steps": steps + 1, "cuts": state["cuts"] + 1}
235	            if reason not in ("stop", "tool_calls", "length"):
236	                drop_live()
237	                raise ModelProviderError(f"The model stopped before finishing its reply (finish reason: {reason}).", detail=f"finish_reason: {reason}")
238	            if pending:
239	                # Text next to tool calls was a note for the person: keep it in the run's history, in order.
240	                if stream is not None:
241	                    stream.commit_narration()
242	                return {"messages": [*conversation, message], "pending": pending, "steps": steps + 1,
243	                        "partial": "", "conts": 0}
244	            written = message.get("content") or ""
245	            if not written.strip() and not partial:
246	                drop_live()
247	                if state["empties"] >= 1:
248	                    raise ModelProviderError("The model returned an empty reply.", detail="empty completion")
249	                return {"messages": [*conversation, {"role": "user", "content": EMPTY_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
250	                        "steps": steps + 1, "empties": state["empties"] + 1}
251	            if reason == "length" and state["conts"] < MAX_CONTINUATIONS and len(partial) + len(written) < MAX_ANSWER_CHARS:
252	                # The answer ran into the output limit: keep what was written and ask for the rest.
253	                return {"messages": [*conversation, message, {"role": "user", "content": CONTINUE_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
254	                        "steps": steps + 1, "partial": partial + written, "conts": state["conts"] + 1}
255	            text = (partial + written).strip()
256	            if schemas and not partial and not state["nudged"] and reason == "stop" and stalled(text):
257	                drop_live()
258	                return {"messages": [*conversation, message, {"role": "user", "content": STALLED_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
259	                        "steps": steps + 1, "nudged": True}
260	            if reason == "length":
261	                text += CUT_OFF_NOTE
262	            if stream is not None:
263	                stream.commit_reply()
264	            return {"messages": [*conversation, message], "pending": [], "steps": steps + 1, "answer": text[:MAX_ANSWER_CHARS]}
265	
266	        async def run_tool(call: dict[str, Any]):
267	            return await gateway.execute(call["function"]["name"], call["function"]["arguments"], call["id"])
268	
269	        def render(call: dict[str, Any], outcome) -> dict[str, Any]:
270	            name = call["function"]["name"]
271	            payload = {"tool": name, **outcome.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"cost_usd", "error_detail"})}
272	            if outcome.status == "error":
273	                if outcome.error_detail:
274	                    payload["detail"] = outcome.error_detail
275	                payload["guidance"] = error_guidance(outcome.error_code)
276	            rendered = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
277	            # Full result is bounded by ToolOutcome. Use an explicitly marked preview when needed, keeping reference ids:
278	            # the same result with its longest texts cut, or, when that cannot fit, the start of its JSON.
279	            fitted = fit_result(payload) if len(rendered.encode()) > RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES else None
280	            if fitted is not None:
281	                rendered = fitted
282	            elif len(rendered.encode()) > RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES:
283	                preview = json.dumps(outcome.data, ensure_ascii=False)
284	                low, high = 0, min(len(preview), 8000)
285	                while low < high:
286	                    middle = (low + high + 1) // 2
287	                    candidate = {**payload, "data": {"preview_truncated": True, "preview": preview[:middle],
288	                        **({"resource_id": outcome.data["resource_id"]} if "resource_id" in outcome.data else {})}}
289	                    if len(json.dumps(candidate, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False).encode()) <= RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES:
290	                        low = middle
291	                    else:
292	                        high = middle - 1
293	                payload["data"] = {"preview_truncated": True, "preview": preview[:low],
294	                    **({"resource_id": outcome.data["resource_id"]} if "resource_id" in outcome.data else {})}
295	                rendered = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
296	            return {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": RESULT_PREFIX + rendered}
297	
298	        def deferred(call: dict[str, Any], allowed: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
299	            detail = (f"Not run: this turn's results would not all fit in the context window. Request at most {allowed} per turn and ask "
300	                      "for this one in a later turn." if allowed else
301	                      "Not run: the context window has no room left for more results. Answer with what you have.")
302	            payload = {"tool": call["function"]["name"], "status": "error", "error_code": "DEFERRED", "detail": detail,
303	                       "guidance": error_guidance("DEFERRED")}
304	            return {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": RESULT_PREFIX + json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)}
305	
306	        async def execute_tools(state: ChildState) -> dict[str, Any]:
307	            calls = state["pending"]
308	            for call in calls:
309	                if not isinstance(call, dict) or call.get("type") != "function":
310	                    raise ModelProviderError("invalid tool call type")
311	                function = call.get("function")
312	                if not isinstance(function, dict) or not isinstance(function.get("name"), str) or not isinstance(function.get("arguments"), str):
313	                    raise ModelProviderError("invalid function call")
314	                if not isinstance(call.get("id"), str):
315	                    raise ModelProviderError("invalid tool call identifier")
316	            replies: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
317	            # Results the model has not read can never be stubbed, so a turn may only run as many calls as
318	            # will fit in the room left. The rest are answered as deferred, not run, so nothing counts as read
319	            # that the model never saw.
320	            room = room_left(state["messages"])
321	            allowed = len(calls) if room is None else min(len(calls), max(0, (room - 400 * len(calls)) // RESULT_TOKENS))
322	            for call in calls[allowed:]:
323	                replies[call["id"]] = deferred(call, allowed)
324	            worked = calls[:allowed]
325	            if len(worked) > 1 and all(getattr(gateway, "is_parallel_safe", lambda _n: False)(call["function"]["name"]) for call in worked):
326	                tasks = [asyncio.ensure_future(run_tool(call)) for call in worked]
327	                try:
328	                    outcomes = list(await asyncio.gather(*tasks))
329	                except BaseException:
330	                    for task in tasks:
331	                        task.cancel()
332	                    await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
333	                    raise
334	            else:
335	                outcomes = [await run_tool(call) for call in worked]
336	            for call, outcome in zip(worked, outcomes):
337	                replies[call["id"]] = render(call, outcome)
338	            return {"messages": [*state["messages"], *(replies[call["id"]] for call in calls)], "pending": []}
339	
340	        graph = StateGraph(ChildState)
341	        graph.add_node("model", call_model)
342	        graph.add_node("tools", execute_tools)
343	        graph.add_edge(START, "model")
344	        graph.add_conditional_edges("model", lambda s: END if s["answer"] is not None else ("tools" if s["pending"] else "model"))
345	        graph.add_edge("tools", "model")
346	        child = graph.compile()
347	        invoke_config: RunnableConfig = dict(config or {})
348	        invoke_config["recursion_limit"] = RECURSION_LIMIT
349	        # Scope a standalone child thread to the unique run. The parent task thread is metadata, never reused as a
350	        # cross-child conversation key.
351	        configurable = dict(invoke_config.get("configurable") or {})
352	        configurable["thread_id"] = f"{ctx.task_id}:child:{reservation.run_id}"
353	        invoke_config["configurable"] = configurable
354	        try:
355	            async with asyncio.timeout(scope.budget.max_wall_time_sec if getattr(ctx, "depth", 0) else None):
356	                output = await child.ainvoke({"messages": messages, "pending": [], "steps": 0, "cuts": 0, "empties": 0,
357	                                          "answer": None, "partial": "", "conts": 0, "nudged": False},
358	                                         invoke_config)
359	        except BaseException:
360	            # An error or a stop request ends the run without a reply: nothing may stay on screen.
361	            drop_live()
362	            raise
363	        return SubagentResult(status="PASS", summary=output["answer"])

# A final answer that reached the output limit is continued this many times before it is shown with CUT_OFF_NOTE.
MAX_CONTINUATIONS = 2
CONTINUE_NOTICE = "Your reply reached the output length limit. Continue it exactly where it stopped, without repeating anything."
# A reply that ends by announcing a next step ("Let me check the tests:") but makes no tool call has stopped too early.
STALLED_NOTICE = ("Your last message announced a next step but made no tool call, so nothing happened. Do it now, or give your "
                  "final answer if you are done.")
RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES = 16000
# A rendered tool result is capped near 16 KB, which is about this many tokens. A turn may only request as
# many results as fit in the room left in the window.
RESULT_TOKENS = RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES + 1000  # includes dense Unicode, JSON escaping and tool-message overhead
# LangGraph needs a finite recursion limit; this is far beyond any real run.
RECURSION_LIMIT = 1_000_000
# A text value cut to make a result fit keeps at least this much: below it, cutting loses more than it saves.
MIN_KEPT_CHARS = 200
OMITTED_MARK = "…[{} characters omitted]"


class ChildState(TypedDict):
    messages: list[dict[str, Any]]
    pending: list[dict[str, Any]]
    steps: int
    cuts: int      # replies cut off by the output limit so far
    empties: int   # empty replies so far
    answer: str | None
    partial: str   # the start of an answer that reached the output limit and is being continued
    conts: int     # continuations asked for so far
    nudged: bool   # a stalled reply was already sent back once


def stalled(text: str) -> bool:
    """The reply ends by introducing something that never came: its last line ends with a colon."""
    last = text.rstrip().rsplit("\n", 1)[-1].strip()
    return last.endswith(":") and not last.startswith(("|", "#", "-", "*", ">")) and len(last) < 300


def fit_result(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
    """`payload` rendered within RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES by cutting its data's longest text values first, or None when that
    cannot make it fit (many short values), for the caller's cruder preview.

    Every key stays, so cursors (next_offset, next_line) and ids still work, and a note says where the full result is.
    The outcome itself is not changed.
    """
    data = json.loads(json.dumps(payload["data"], ensure_ascii=False))
    leaves: list[list[Any]] = []  # [container, key, original text, characters kept]

    def collect(node: Any) -> None:
        items = node.items() if isinstance(node, dict) else enumerate(node) if isinstance(node, list) else ()
        for key, value in items:
            if isinstance(value, str):
                leaves.append([node, key, value, len(value)])
            else:
                collect(value)
    collect(data)
    reference = data.get("resource_id")
    note = "This result was too long to show whole, so its longest text values were cut where marked."
    if isinstance(reference, str):
        note += (f' Read the full result with read_context_resource(resource_id="{reference}", offset=0) when that tool is '
                 "available, continuing from its next_offset; this does not repeat the original call.")
    for _ in range(200):
        rendered = json.dumps({**payload, "data": {**data, "preview_truncated": True, "preview_note": note}},
                              ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
        excess = len(rendered.encode()) - RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES
        if excess <= 0:
            return rendered
        leaf = max(leaves, key=lambda item: item[3], default=None)
        if leaf is None or leaf[3] <= MIN_KEPT_CHARS:
            return None
        container, key, original, kept = leaf
        # Characters to drop for `excess` bytes at this value's own bytes per character (escaping, Unicode), plus the mark.
        size = len(json.dumps(original[:kept], ensure_ascii=False).encode())
        leaf[3] = kept = max(MIN_KEPT_CHARS, kept - int(excess * kept / max(1, size)) - 40)
        container[key] = original[:kept] + OMITTED_MARK.format(len(original) - kept)
    return None


class ChildRuntime:
    async def run(self, *, definition: AgentDefinition, ctx: TaskContext,
                  scope: EffectiveScope, model: ToolCallingModel, gateway: ToolGateway,
                  budgets: BudgetService, reservation: Reservation,
                  messages: list[dict[str, Any]], resources: ResourceResolver,
                  reauthorize: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]],
                  config: RunnableConfig | None = None, stream=None) -> SubagentResult:
        schemas = gateway.schemas()

        def drop_live() -> None:
            """Whatever the sink shows is not going to be used (an attempt thrown away, a run that failed): clear it."""
            discard = getattr(stream, "discard", None)
            if discard is not None:
                discard()

        # Models that retry a broken stream themselves say so by taking `on_retry`; others are simply not told.
        accepts_retry = "on_retry" in inspect.signature(model.complete).parameters
        accepts_tool = "on_tool" in inspect.signature(model.complete).parameters
        context_budget = getattr(model, "context_budget_tokens", None)
        max_input = getattr(model, "max_input_tokens", None)

        def room_left(conversation: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int | None:
            """Input tokens still free once every result the model has already read is stubbed out."""
            if not max_input:
                return None
            return max_input - conservative_input_tokens(compact_messages(conversation, 1, 0), schemas)

        def fit(conversation: list[dict[str, Any]]):
            """The messages to send and their cost bound: compact gently, then harder, until the request fits."""
            for keep in (KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS, 1, 0):
                sent = compact_messages(conversation, context_budget if keep == KEEP_RECENT_RESULTS else 1, keep)
                try:
                    return sent, model.maximum_request_cost(sent, schemas)
                except ModelContextLimit:
                    continue
            return None

        async def call_model(state: ChildState) -> dict[str, Any]:
            await reauthorize()
            budgets.check_active(reservation.id)
            steps = state["steps"]
            conversation = state["messages"]
            fitted = fit(conversation)
            if fitted is None:
                raise ModelContextLimit("The conversation no longer fits in the model's context window, even with old tool results removed.")
            sent, bound = fitted
            stubbed = [kept.get("tool_call_id") for original, kept in zip(conversation, sent)
                       if original is not kept and kept.get("role") == "tool"]
            operation_key = f"{reservation.run_id}:model:{steps}"
            auditor = getattr(resources, "record_provider_input", None)
            if auditor is not None:
                await auditor(ctx, operation_key, sent, schemas)
            budgets.authorize_operation(reservation.id, operation_key, bound, kind="model")
            extra: dict[str, Any] = {}
            partial = state["partial"]
            broken = 0

            def restart() -> None:
                # A new attempt (or a retried, broken one) starts from the part of the answer already written.
                stream.begin()
                if partial:
                    stream.feed(partial)

            def retried() -> None:
                # A stream that broke midway was billed for what it produced, which the provider never reported, so the
                # ledger records that attempt as its own operation of unknown cost before the request is sent again.
                nonlocal broken
                broken += 1
                key = f"{operation_key}:broken:{broken}"
                budgets.authorize_operation(reservation.id, key, bound, kind="model")
                budgets.record_usage(reservation.id, key, None)
                if stream is not None:
                    restart()
            if accepts_retry:
                extra["on_retry"] = retried
            if stream is not None:
                extra["on_text"] = stream.feed
                extra["on_narration"] = stream.feed_narration
                if accepts_tool and getattr(stream, "feed_tool", None) is not None:
                    # A call is shown as the model writes it, under the id its tool.started event will carry.
                    extra["on_tool"] = lambda index, provider_id, name, piece: stream.feed_tool(
                        index, legacy_call_id(f"{reservation.run_id}:tool:{provider_id}"), name, piece)
                restart()
            try:
                response = await model.complete(sent, schemas, **extra)
            except BaseException:
                budgets.record_usage(reservation.id, operation_key, None)
                drop_live()
                raise
            # The call succeeded, so its real cost is recorded before anything else can fail: `end` may raise an event
            # error the sink deferred (a stopped run, a lost lease), which must not charge the call's upper bound.
            budgets.record_usage(reservation.id, operation_key, response.usage.cost_usd,
                usage={"input_tokens": response.usage.input_tokens,
                       "output_tokens": response.usage.output_tokens, "compacted_results": len(stubbed),
                       "configured_model": model.model_id, "reported_model": response.model_id})
            if stream is not None:
                try:
                    stream.end()
                except BaseException:
                    drop_live()
                    raise
            message = response.message
            if len(json.dumps(message, allow_nan=False).encode()) > 4 * MAX_ANSWER_CHARS or message.get("role") != "assistant":
                raise ModelProviderError("invalid model response envelope")
            pending = message.get("tool_calls") or []
            if not isinstance(pending, list):
                raise ModelProviderError("invalid model tool calls")
            if len({call.get("id") for call in pending if isinstance(call, dict)}) != len(pending):
                raise ModelProviderError("duplicate model tool call identifiers")
            reason = response.finish_reason
            if reason == "length" and pending:
                # Cut off while writing tool calls: their arguments are unusable. Ask again, shorter.
                drop_live()
                if state["cuts"] >= MAX_CUTOFF_RETRIES:
                    raise ModelProviderError("The model kept running out of output space while calling tools.", detail="finish_reason: length")
                return {"messages": [*conversation, {"role": "user", "content": CUTOFF_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
                        "steps": steps + 1, "cuts": state["cuts"] + 1}
            if reason not in ("stop", "tool_calls", "length"):
                drop_live()
                raise ModelProviderError(f"The model stopped before finishing its reply (finish reason: {reason}).", detail=f"finish_reason: {reason}")
            if pending:
                # Text next to tool calls was a note for the person: keep it in the run's history, in order.
                if stream is not None:
                    stream.commit_narration()
                return {"messages": [*conversation, message], "pending": pending, "steps": steps + 1,
                        "partial": "", "conts": 0}
            written = message.get("content") or ""
            if not written.strip() and not partial:
                drop_live()
                if state["empties"] >= 1:
                    raise ModelProviderError("The model returned an empty reply.", detail="empty completion")
                return {"messages": [*conversation, {"role": "user", "content": EMPTY_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
                        "steps": steps + 1, "empties": state["empties"] + 1}
            if reason == "length" and state["conts"] < MAX_CONTINUATIONS and len(partial) + len(written) < MAX_ANSWER_CHARS:
                # The answer ran into the output limit: keep what was written and ask for the rest.
                return {"messages": [*conversation, message, {"role": "user", "content": CONTINUE_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
                        "steps": steps + 1, "partial": partial + written, "conts": state["conts"] + 1}
            text = (partial + written).strip()
            if schemas and not partial and not state["nudged"] and reason == "stop" and stalled(text):
                drop_live()
                return {"messages": [*conversation, message, {"role": "user", "content": STALLED_NOTICE}], "pending": [],
                        "steps": steps + 1, "nudged": True}
            if reason == "length":
                text += CUT_OFF_NOTE
            if stream is not None:
                stream.commit_reply()
            return {"messages": [*conversation, message], "pending": [], "steps": steps + 1, "answer": text[:MAX_ANSWER_CHARS]}

        async def run_tool(call: dict[str, Any]):
            return await gateway.execute(call["function"]["name"], call["function"]["arguments"], call["id"])

        def render(call: dict[str, Any], outcome) -> dict[str, Any]:
            name = call["function"]["name"]
            payload = {"tool": name, **outcome.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"cost_usd", "error_detail"})}
            if outcome.status == "error":
                if outcome.error_detail:
                    payload["detail"] = outcome.error_detail
                payload["guidance"] = error_guidance(outcome.error_code)
            rendered = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
            # Full result is bounded by ToolOutcome. Use an explicitly marked preview when needed, keeping reference ids:
            # the same result with its longest texts cut, or, when that cannot fit, the start of its JSON.
            fitted = fit_result(payload) if len(rendered.encode()) > RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES else None
            if fitted is not None:
                rendered = fitted
            elif len(rendered.encode()) > RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES:
                preview = json.dumps(outcome.data, ensure_ascii=False)
                low, high = 0, min(len(preview), 8000)
                while low < high:
                    middle = (low + high + 1) // 2
                    candidate = {**payload, "data": {"preview_truncated": True, "preview": preview[:middle],
                        **({"resource_id": outcome.data["resource_id"]} if "resource_id" in outcome.data else {})}}
                    if len(json.dumps(candidate, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False).encode()) <= RESULT_PREVIEW_BYTES:
                        low = middle
                    else:
                        high = middle - 1
                payload["data"] = {"preview_truncated": True, "preview": preview[:low],
                    **({"resource_id": outcome.data["resource_id"]} if "resource_id" in outcome.data else {})}
                rendered = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)
            return {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": RESULT_PREFIX + rendered}

        def deferred(call: dict[str, Any], allowed: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
            detail = (f"Not run: this turn's results would not all fit in the context window. Request at most {allowed} per turn and ask "
                      "for this one in a later turn." if allowed else
                      "Not run: the context window has no room left for more results. Answer with what you have.")
            payload = {"tool": call["function"]["name"], "status": "error", "error_code": "DEFERRED", "detail": detail,
                       "guidance": error_guidance("DEFERRED")}
            return {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": call["id"], "content": RESULT_PREFIX + json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)}

        async def execute_tools(state: ChildState) -> dict[str, Any]:
            calls = state["pending"]
            for call in calls:
                if not isinstance(call, dict) or call.get("type") != "function":
                    raise ModelProviderError("invalid tool call type")
                function = call.get("function")
                if not isinstance(function, dict) or not isinstance(function.get("name"), str) or not isinstance(function.get("arguments"), str):
                    raise ModelProviderError("invalid function call")
                if not isinstance(call.get("id"), str):
                    raise ModelProviderError("invalid tool call identifier")
            replies: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
            # Results the model has not read can never be stubbed, so a turn may only run as many calls as
            # will fit in the room left. The rest are answered as deferred, not run, so nothing counts as read
            # that the model never saw.
            room = room_left(state["messages"])
            allowed = len(calls) if room is None else min(len(calls), max(0, (room - 400 * len(calls)) // RESULT_TOKENS))
            for call in calls[allowed:]:
                replies[call["id"]] = deferred(call, allowed)
            worked = calls[:allowed]
            if len(worked) > 1 and all(getattr(gateway, "is_parallel_safe", lambda _n: False)(call["function"]["name"]) for call in worked):
                tasks = [asyncio.ensure_future(run_tool(call)) for call in worked]
                try:
                    outcomes = list(await asyncio.gather(*tasks))
                except BaseException:
                    for task in tasks:
                        task.cancel()
                    await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
                    raise
            else:
                outcomes = [await run_tool(call) for call in worked]
            for call, outcome in zip(worked, outcomes):
                replies[call["id"]] = render(call, outcome)
            return {"messages": [*state["messages"], *(replies[call["id"]] for call in calls)], "pending": []}

        graph = StateGraph(ChildState)
        graph.add_node("model", call_model)
        graph.add_node("tools", execute_tools)
        graph.add_edge(START, "model")
        graph.add_conditional_edges("model", lambda s: END if s["answer"] is not None else ("tools" if s["pending"] else "model"))
        graph.add_edge("tools", "model")
        child = graph.compile()
        invoke_config: RunnableConfig = dict(config or {})
        invoke_config["recursion_limit"] = RECURSION_LIMIT
        # Scope a standalone child thread to the unique run. The parent task thread is metadata, never reused as a
        # cross-child conversation key.
        configurable = dict(invoke_config.get("configurable") or {})
        configurable["thread_id"] = f"{ctx.task_id}:child:{reservation.run_id}"
        invoke_config["configurable"] = configurable
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(scope.budget.max_wall_time_sec if getattr(ctx, "depth", 0) else None):
                output = await child.ainvoke({"messages": messages, "pending": [], "steps": 0, "cuts": 0, "empties": 0,
                                          "answer": None, "partial": "", "conts": 0, "nudged": False},
                                         invoke_config)
        except BaseException:
            # An error or a stop request ends the run without a reply: nothing may stay on screen.
            drop_live()
            raise
        return SubagentResult(status="PASS", summary=output["answer"])

1	"""AsyncOpenAI Chat Completions adapter with measured usage and bounded, cost-safe retries.
2	
3	Official contracts reviewed:
4	https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/python
5	https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/python/resources/chat/subresources/completions/methods/create
6	
7	The SDK's own retries stay disabled; this adapter does its own, bounded and visible. It retries failures that
8	produced no completion (rate limits, 5xx, failed or dropped connections, timeouts, transient error frames sent
9	mid-stream), with jittered backoff that honours the provider's retry-after. A stream that breaks (or simply ends
10	without a finish reason) after it started is retried too, since repeating one request costs far less than failing
11	the whole run; `on_retry` tells the caller to throw away what it showed.
12	Quota and credential errors are never retried.
13	
14	Reasoning effort is chosen per person and applied per run (`with_reasoning_effort`). Without reasoning the Chat
15	Completions endpoint serves every request, exactly as it always did. A model whose Chat Completions endpoint takes function
16	calls only without reasoning (gpt-6-luna, see `effort.py`) is sent through the Responses endpoint when an effort is asked
17	for. The runtime keeps speaking the chat message format either way: this adapter translates the history it is given into
18	Responses input and the reply back into one assistant message, so nothing above it changes.
19	"""

131	def message_from_response(response: Any) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], str]:

171	def _response_error(error: Any) -> Exception:
172	    """A failed response (or an `error` event) as the error the adapter already knows how to classify and retry."""
173	    code = getattr(error, "code", None)
174	    text = getattr(error, "message", None) or "the model provider reported an error"
175	    if code == "context_length_exceeded":
